title: EPA 608 Core practice test
description: Free EPA Section 608 Core practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the EPA page or the section of 40 CFR Part 82 it comes from.

questions.question: Under EPA's Section 608 program, which description fits a "small appliance"?

options.A: Any appliance that plugs into a standard household outlet
options.B: An appliance fully manufactured, charged and hermetically sealed in a factory with five pounds or less of refrigerant
options.C: Any air conditioner with a charge under 50 pounds
options.D: An appliance that uses a low-pressure refrigerant

questions.explanation: EPA defines a small appliance by how it is built and charged: fully manufactured, charged and hermetically sealed in a factory with five pounds or less of refrigerant. Plug type, a 50-pound charge or the refrigerant's pressure class do not define it.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Under EPA's sales restriction, refrigerant for use in an appliance may be sold only to a buyer who:

options.B: Is, or employs, a certified technician
options.C: Buys at least one full cylinder
options.D: Signs a statement promising not to vent the refrigerant

questions.explanation: EPA states it is a violation to sell or distribute refrigerant for use in an appliance unless the recipient is, or employs, a certified technician. Sellers must verify this. A business license or a signed promise does not satisfy the rule.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Before used refrigerant recovered from an appliance can be sold to a new owner, what must happen to it?

options.A: It must be filtered through a liquid-line drier
options.B: It must be stored for 30 days
options.C: It must be reclaimed by an EPA-certified reclaimer
options.D: It must be mixed with new refrigerant of the same type

questions.explanation: EPA states that if recovered refrigerant changes ownership, it must be reclaimed by an EPA-certified refrigerant reclaimer. Filtering or mixing it yourself does not meet that requirement.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: Recovered refrigerant may be charged back into equipment without being reclaimed when the equipment:

options.A: Is owned by the same person who owned the system it came from
options.B: Is less than five years old
options.D: Belongs to any customer of the same technician

questions.explanation: EPA allows recovered refrigerant to go back into the same system, or into other systems owned by the same person, without restriction. If the refrigerant changes ownership, for example to another customer, it must be reclaimed first.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: Where does EPA require a certified technician to keep a copy of their Section 608 certification?

options.A: In the service vehicle at all times
options.B: With the state licensing board
options.D: Posted on every appliance they service

questions.explanation: EPA requires technicians to keep a copy of their certification at their place of business. EPA does not require the card to be carried while servicing equipment.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: How long must a technician keep a copy of their Section 608 certification?

options.A: Until three years after they are no longer operating as a technician
options.B: For one year after the test date
options.C: For five years after the test date
options.D: Only until they receive the plastic card

questions.explanation: EPA says to keep the copy until three years after you are no longer operating as a technician. The rule is tied to when you stop working as a technician, not to the test date.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: How often must Section 608 technician certification be renewed?

options.B: Every five years
options.D: Never, because the credentials do not expire

questions.explanation: EPA states that Section 608 technician certification credentials do not expire, so there is no renewal cycle.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Requirements

questions.question: A technician has lost their Section 608 certification card. Who should they contact for a replacement?

options.B: The company that certified them, whose name is on the card
options.C: The refrigerant wholesaler where they buy refrigerant
options.D: Their state environmental agency

questions.explanation: EPA does not administer the tests or issue cards, and it does not keep a database of certified technicians. EPA tells technicians to contact the company that certified them, whose name appears on the card.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: What must a technician do to receive Universal certification?

options.B: Work under supervision for two years
options.C: Pass the examinations at all levels
options.D: Pass Type II and Type III only

questions.explanation: EPA states that to receive Universal certification, an individual must pass the examinations at all levels.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Under EPA's regulations, how long do testing organizations have to issue test results after the date of the test?

options.B: Up to 30 days
options.D: Up to 1 year

questions.explanation: EPA notes that its regulations allow testing organizations up to 30 days from the date of the test to issue test results.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Who issues Section 608 test results and certification cards?

options.B: The test proctor at the end of the exam
options.C: The EPA-approved testing and certification organization that gave the test
options.D: The technician's employer

questions.explanation: EPA states that it does not administer the tests and does not issue test results or certification cards, and that proctors may not issue certification cards. Results and cards come from the EPA-approved testing and certification organization.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Under EPA's rules, how long may a person work as an apprentice from the date of first registering?

options.B: One year
options.D: There is no limit

questions.explanation: EPA states that a person may only be an apprentice for two years from the date of first registering.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Is Section 608 certification needed to add or remove refrigerant from a mini-split system as part of installation?

options.B: Only if the system holds more than 50 pounds
options.D: Yes, Section 608 technician certification is required

questions.explanation: EPA states that adding or removing refrigerant from a mini-split as part of installation requires Section 608 technician certification.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: Section 608 technician certification is required to dispose of appliances, except for which type of appliance?

options.B: High-pressure appliances
options.D: Commercial refrigeration

questions.explanation: EPA states that technician certification is required to dispose of appliances, except for small appliances (and motor vehicle air conditioners or MVAC-like appliances). High-pressure, low-pressure and commercial systems need a certified technician.

source.title: EPA: Questions and Answers for Section 608 Certified Technicians

questions.question: For equipment that enters the waste stream with its charge intact, such as household refrigerators and freezers or window air conditioners, who is responsible for ensuring the refrigerant is recovered before final disposal?

options.B: The final person in the disposal chain
options.D: The last technician who serviced the appliance

questions.explanation: EPA places the responsibility on the final person in the disposal chain to ensure refrigerant is recovered from this equipment before its final disposal. The people who recover refrigerant from small appliances, MVACs and MVAC-like appliances do not have to be certified technicians.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Safe Disposal Requirements

questions.question: When the final disposer relies on a signed statement from the person dropping off an appliance, what must that statement include?

options.A: The appliance's serial number and purchase date
options.B: A sticker number issued by EPA
options.C: The name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant and the date it was recovered
options.D: The weight of the appliance

questions.explanation: EPA requires the signed statement to include the name and address of the person who recovered the refrigerant and the date it was recovered. EPA does not mandate or accept a sticker as verification.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Safe Disposal Requirements

questions.question: Except for equipment manufactured before November 15, 1993, recovery or recycling equipment must be certified by:

options.B: The technician who uses it
options.D: A state fire marshal

questions.explanation: EPA states that, except for equipment manufactured before November 15, 1993, recovery or recycling equipment must have been certified by an EPA-approved equipment testing organization, and must be used according to the manufacturer's directions.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: When changing refrigerant oil, EPA says it is a violation to change the oil at a pressure higher than:

options.B: 5 psig
options.D: 25 psig

questions.explanation: EPA states it is a violation to change oil at higher than 5 psig. The appliance, or the receiver the oil drains into, must first be evacuated or pressurized to no more than 5 psig.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: If leaking equipment cannot be evacuated to the required level, the leaking components must be evacuated to the lowest attainable level, which cannot exceed:

options.B: 5 psig
options.D: 29.9 inches of mercury vacuum

questions.explanation: For leaking equipment, EPA says to isolate leaking components where possible, evacuate non-leaking components to the specified levels, and evacuate leaking components to the lowest level attainable without substantially contaminating the refrigerant. That level cannot exceed 0 psig.

source.title: EPA: Stationary Refrigeration Service Practice Requirements

questions.question: Which of these does EPA give as an example of a refrigerant that is exempt from the refrigerant management requirements?
questions.explanation: EPA's technician fact sheet gives carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water as examples of exempt refrigerants, and points to 40 CFR 82.154(a) for the full list. R-22, R-12 and R-410A are not among those examples.

source.title: EPA fact sheet: Refrigerant Management Requirements, What Technicians Need to Know

questions.question: Which element in CFC and HCFC refrigerants is responsible for destroying stratospheric ozone?

options.B: Hydrogen
options.D: Chlorine

questions.explanation: EPA's Core test topics list the destruction of ozone by chlorine and the presence of chlorine in CFC and HCFC refrigerants. HFCs contain no chlorine.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: How do CFC, HCFC and HFC refrigerants compare in ozone-depletion potential (ODP)?

options.A: CFCs are higher than HCFCs, which are higher than HFCs
options.B: HFCs are higher than HCFCs, which are higher than CFCs
options.C: HCFCs are higher than CFCs, which are higher than HFCs
options.D: All three have the same ODP

questions.explanation: EPA's test topics state the idea that CFCs have a higher ozone-depletion potential than HCFCs, which in turn have a higher ODP than HFCs.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: According to EPA's test topics, which gas should be used for leak detection instead of oxygen or compressed air?

options.B: Hydrogen
options.D: Acetylene

questions.explanation: EPA's Core safety topics include the use of nitrogen rather than oxygen or compressed air for leak detection, together with a pressure regulator and relief valve.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: When pressurizing a system with nitrogen for leak testing, what equipment do EPA's test topics call for?

options.A: A vacuum pump and micron gauge
options.B: A pressure regulator and a relief valve
options.D: A refrigerant identifier

questions.explanation: EPA's Core safety topics include the use of a pressure regulator and relief valve with nitrogen.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: EPA's test topics warn of the risks of filling refrigerant cylinders more than what percent full?

options.B: 65 percent
options.D: 100 percent

questions.explanation: EPA's Core safety topics include the risks of filling cylinders more than 80 percent full, and the difference between reusable recovery cylinders and disposable cylinders.

source.title: EPA: Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics

questions.question: Under the Section 608 rules, a medium-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure at 104 °F of:

options.B: Between 45 psia and 170 psia
options.D: Above 355 psia

questions.explanation: The rule defines a medium-pressure appliance as one using a refrigerant with a liquid phase saturation pressure "between 45 psia and 170 psia at 104 °F." Below 45 psia is the low-pressure range, and 170 to 355 psia is the high-pressure range.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which refrigerant does the rule list as an example for a low-pressure appliance?
questions.explanation: The low-pressure appliance definition lists examples including "R-11, R-123, R-113, and R-245fa." The rule lists R-410A as a high-pressure example, R-134a as a medium-pressure example and R-23 as a very high-pressure example.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A very high-pressure appliance uses a refrigerant that has which property?

options.A: A liquid phase saturation pressure between 45 psia and 170 psia at 104 °F
options.B: A liquid phase saturation pressure below 45 psia at 104 °F
options.C: A boiling point above 104 °F at atmospheric pressure
options.D: A critical temperature below 104 °F or a liquid phase saturation pressure above 355 psia at 104 °F

questions.explanation: The rule defines a very high-pressure appliance as one using a refrigerant "with a critical temperature below 104 °F" or with a liquid phase saturation pressure above 355 psia at 104 °F. The 45 to 170 psia range describes medium-pressure appliances, and below 45 psia describes low-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In the Section 608 rules, what does it mean to "recover" refrigerant?

options.A: To remove refrigerant in any condition from an appliance and store it in an external container
options.B: To clean refrigerant for reuse in equipment of the same owner
options.C: To reprocess refrigerant to the purity specifications in appendix A
options.D: To return refrigerant to its manufacturer for destruction

questions.explanation: To recover means "to remove refrigerant in any condition from an appliance" and store it in an external container, without necessarily testing or processing it. Cleaning for reuse by the same owner is the definition of recycle, and reprocessing to appendix A specifications is reclaim.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which description matches the rule's definition of "reclaim"?

options.A: Removing refrigerant from an appliance and storing it without testing it
options.B: Reprocessing recovered refrigerant to the appendix A specifications and verifying it meets them
options.C: Cleaning refrigerant with filter-driers for reuse in the same owner's equipment
options.D: Moving refrigerant from one appliance to another at the same site

questions.explanation: Reclaim means to reprocess recovered refrigerant to all of the appendix A specifications (based on AHRI Standard 700-2016) and to verify it meets them using the prescribed analytical method. Cleaning for reuse by the same owner without meeting all reclamation requirements is recycling, not reclaiming.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An MVAC-like appliance, such as the air conditioning on a farm tractor, has a full charge of how much refrigerant?

options.B: 50 pounds or more
options.D: 2 pounds or less

questions.explanation: The rule defines an MVAC-like appliance as an open-drive compressor appliance "with a full charge of 20 pounds or less of refrigerant" used to cool the compartment of off-road vehicles or equipment. It names agricultural and construction vehicles as examples.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does the definition of "appliance" treat a system that has multiple independent refrigerant circuits?

options.A: The whole system counts as one appliance
options.B: Only the largest circuit counts as an appliance
options.C: The system counts as an appliance only if all circuits share a compressor
options.D: Each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance

questions.explanation: The appliance definition states: "each independent circuit is considered a separate appliance." The rule does not treat the whole multi-circuit system as a single appliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the definition of "technician," which activity is reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit?

options.B: Painting the appliance
options.D: Tightening nuts and bolts

questions.explanation: The technician definition lists "cutting the refrigerant line" among activities reasonably expected to violate the integrity of the refrigerant circuit. Painting the appliance, rewiring an external electrical circuit and tightening nuts and bolts are listed as activities not reasonably expected to do so.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the rule's definition, connecting and disconnecting hoses and gauges to measure pressures is:

options.A: Considered opening an appliance in all cases
options.B: Not considered "opening an appliance"
options.C: Considered opening an appliance only on low-pressure appliances
options.D: Considered opening an appliance if the hoses stay connected for more than 15 minutes

questions.explanation: "Opening an appliance" means any maintenance, service, repair or disposal that would release refrigerant to the atmosphere. The rule states that connecting and disconnecting hoses and gauges to measure pressures, add refrigerant, or recover refrigerant "are not considered 'opening an appliance.'"

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides removing a compressor, condenser, evaporator or auxiliary heat exchange coil, which work counts as "major" maintenance, service or repair?

options.A: Uncovering any opening for more than 5 minutes
options.B: Uncovering an opening of more than 1 square inch of flow area for more than 60 minutes
options.C: Uncovering an opening of more than 4 square inches of flow area for more than 15 minutes
options.D: Uncovering an opening of more than 10 square inches of flow area for any length of time

questions.explanation: Major maintenance, service or repair includes work that involves "uncovering an opening of more than four (4) square inches" of flow area for more than 15 minutes. The other size and time combinations do not appear in the definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A technician recovers a non-exempt refrigerant into a cylinder and later knowingly releases it outdoors. Under the rule, this release is:

options.A: Allowed, because the refrigerant was already removed from the appliance
options.B: Allowed as a de minimis release
options.C: Allowed if certified recovery equipment was used
options.D: A violation of the venting prohibition

questions.explanation: The rule states that the knowing release of a class I, class II or non-exempt substitute refrigerant "after its recovery from an appliance is a violation of the venting prohibition." Having already recovered the refrigerant does not make a later release acceptable.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which kind of refrigerant release is not subject to the venting prohibition?

options.A: De minimis releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerant
options.B: Any release of refrigerant that took place after it was recovered
options.C: Releases made to shorten a service call
options.D: Any release from an appliance that is being disposed of

questions.explanation: The rule says "de minimis releases associated with good faith attempts to recycle or recover refrigerants" are not subject to the prohibition, provided the required practices are followed. A knowing release after recovery is specifically named as a violation, and the prohibition covers disposal as well as service.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In which uses is ammonia an exempt substitute under the venting prohibition?

options.B: In commercial or industrial process refrigeration or in absorption units
options.D: Only in motor vehicle air conditioners

questions.explanation: The list of exempt substitutes includes "Ammonia in commercial or industrial process refrigeration or in absorption units." Unlike carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water, ammonia is not exempt "in any application."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A seller of non-exempt refrigerant must keep invoices showing the purchaser's name, date of sale and quantity. How long must these records be kept?

options.B: Two years
options.D: Five years

questions.explanation: Sellers must keep invoices that indicate the purchaser's name, the date of sale and the quantity purchased, and "All records must be kept for three years." The rule does not set a one-, two- or five-year period for these invoices.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In which case may used refrigerant be sold or transferred for use as a refrigerant without first being reclaimed by a certified reclaimer?

options.A: When it is sold to any business that owns appliances
options.B: When it has passed once through a filter-drier
options.C: When it is sold by a technician to a different customer
options.D: When it is transferred between a parent company and one of its subsidiaries

questions.explanation: Among the exceptions to the rule on selling used refrigerant is refrigerant "being transferred between or among a parent company" and one or more of its subsidiaries. Selling to an unrelated buyer is not one of the listed exceptions, so that refrigerant would have to be reclaimed first.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.154, Prohibitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A certified reclaimer may release no more than what percent of the refrigerant during the reclamation process?

options.B: 0.5 percent
options.D: 5 percent

questions.explanation: Persons reclaiming used refrigerant for sale to a new owner must "Release no more than 1.5 percent of the refrigerant during the reclamation process." The other percentages do not appear in the reclaimer requirements.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: By what date must reclaimers send EPA their annual report on the material they received and the refrigerant they reclaimed?

options.A: December 31 of the same calendar year
options.B: February 1 of the next calendar year
options.C: July 30 of the next calendar year
options.D: April 15 of the next calendar year

questions.explanation: Reclaimers must report to EPA "annually by February 1 of the next calendar year." The report covers the material sent to them by refrigerant type, the mass of each refrigerant reclaimed and the mass of waste products.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When a refrigerant reclamation business changes owners, what does the rule require of the new owner?

options.A: Nothing, because the old certificate transfers with the business
options.B: To certify with EPA within one year
options.C: To certify with EPA within 30 days of the change
options.D: To certify with EPA within 90 days of the change

questions.explanation: The rule states "Certificates are not transferable," and the new owner must certify with EPA within 30 days of the change in ownership. So the old owner's certificate does not carry over to the new owner.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.164, Reclaimer certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For reclamation purposes, what does the rule mean by a "batch" of refrigerant?

options.A: All refrigerant a reclaimer receives in one calendar month
options.B: All refrigerant recovered from one appliance
options.C: One shipment of recovered refrigerant sent by a technician
options.D: A single bulk cylinder of refrigerant after all reclamation is complete, before packaging or shipping

questions.explanation: A batch is defined as "a single bulk cylinder of refrigerant after all reclamation has been completed" prior to packaging or shipping to the market. It is not defined by time period, by appliance or by incoming shipment.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.152, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which certification type is required to maintain, service, repair or dispose of low-pressure appliances?

options.B: Type I
options.D: No certification is required

questions.explanation: The rule says persons who work on or dispose of low-pressure appliances "must be certified as Type III technicians." Type I covers small appliances, and Type II covers medium-, high- and very high-pressure appliances.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Technicians who maintain, service or repair MVAC-like appliances must hold which certification?

options.B: Type II, or certification under 40 CFR part 82, subpart B
options.D: No certification, because MVAC-like appliances are exempt

questions.explanation: The rule says technicians who service MVAC-like appliances "must either be certified as Type II technicians" or be certified under 40 CFR part 82, subpart B. Only the disposal of MVAC-like appliances is exempt from certification, not their service or repair.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under what condition is a registered apprentice exempt from the technician certification requirement?

options.A: When the apprentice has passed the Core section only
options.B: When the apprentice works only on weekends
options.C: When the apprentice is closely and continually supervised by a certified technician
options.D: When the apprentice's employer files a notice with EPA

questions.explanation: Apprentices are exempt provided the apprentice "is closely and continually supervised by a certified technician" during work that could release refrigerant. The rule also makes both the supervising technician and the apprentice responsible for the apprentice's compliance.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A person wants to take the certification test orally. How must they request this?

options.A: By asking the proctor on the day of the test
options.B: By phone at least 10 days before the test
options.C: By writing to EPA at least 60 days before the test
options.D: In writing to the program at least 30 days before the test, explaining why

questions.explanation: A test may be given orally to anyone who requests it "in writing, to the program at least 30 days before" the scheduled exam, and the request must explain why it is being made. The request goes to the certification program, not to EPA or the proctor on test day.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 82.161, Technician certification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How many questions from Group 1 (the Core group) does each Section 608 certification test include?
questions.explanation: Appendix D states that "Each test must include 25 questions drawn from Group 1" plus 25 from each relevant technical group. The figure of 100 is the total length of a Universal test, not the number of Core questions.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What is the passing score for the closed-book Type I, Type II, Type III and Universal certification tests?

options.B: 70 percent
options.D: 80 percent

questions.explanation: Appendix D sets the passing score for the closed-book tests at "70 percent." The 84 percent score applies only to Type I tests taken in the mail-in format.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR Part 82, Subpart F, Appendix D (as of Nov 3, 2026)
